message.content: {"research_brief": "How can I reconstruct the Internet Research Agency’s 2016 social-media influence operation by linking, using only evidence returned by the benchmark tools, (1) facts alleged in relevant U.S. Department of Justice indictments, (2) findings and assessments in Senate investigative materials, (3) platform-provided data, (4) identified or alleged online personas, accounts, organizations, and operators, (5) funding sources, payment mechanisms, and organizational relationships, and (6) stated or inferred campaign objectives, tactics, audiences, timelines, and outcomes—while distinguishing documented facts from allegations, assessments, inferences, and unresolved uncertainty; avoiding invented facts and unsupported IDs or relationship names; citing every substantive assertion only with source IDs returned by the tools; identifying corroboration, gaps, and contradictions; and returning a complete readable Markdown report without asking whether to continue, followed by a fenced JSON object containing exactly the arrays `findings`, `claims`, `reasoning_steps`, and `contradictions`, where each finding includes `question`, `answer`, `supporting_entities`, and `source_references`, each claim includes `claim` and `source_references`, each reasoning step includes `id`, `conclusion`, `premise_entities`, and `premise_relations`, and each contradiction includes `contradiction_id`, `description`, and `source_references`?"}
